entities.summary:
The president of Germany, officially titled the federal president of the Federal Republic of Germany, is the head of state of Germany. The current officeholder is Frank-Walter Steinmeier who was elected on 12 February 2017 and re-elected on 13 February 2022. He is currently serving his second five-year-term, which began on 19 March 2022.

The president serves as the formal representative of the Federal Republic of Germany in international relations, and is also the commander-in-chief of the German Armed Forces. The office of the president is largely ceremonial, but the president also has some powers, such as the ability to dissolve the Bundestag and call new elections.

The significance of the president of Germany lies in the country's transition from a post-war occupied zone to a sovereign state. The president has played a crucial role in establishing Germany's position in the international community and has served as a symbol of national unity.

The president of Germany has been a figure of great importance in the country's history, with many notable presidents leaving a lasting impact on the nation. For example, Theodor Heuss, who served as president from 1949 to 1959, was a key figure in Germany's post-war reconstruction and played a significant role in the country's integration into the European Community.
